In current LlamaIndex (the `llama-index-core` package, v0.10 and later), you set the global defaults through the `Settings` object in `llama_index.core`. Any index, query engine, or retriever you create afterward uses these defaults unless you pass its own models explicitly.

```python
from llama_index.core import Settings
from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI
from llama_index.embeddings.openai import OpenAIEmbedding

Settings.llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0.1)
Settings.embed_model = OpenAIEmbedding(model="text-embedding-3-small")
```

Install the integration packages separately:

```
pip install llama-index-core llama-index-llms-openai llama-index-embeddings-openai
```

The OpenAI classes read `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment. In PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-..."
```

To use local models, swap in other integrations and assign them the same way. For example, with Ollama and HuggingFace:

```python
from llama_index.llms.ollama import Ollama
from llama_index.embeddings.huggingface import HuggingFaceEmbedding

Settings.llm = Ollama(model="llama3.1", request_timeout=120.0)
Settings.embed_model = HuggingFaceEmbedding(model_name="BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5")
```

Set these before building indexes. Models are resolved when objects are constructed, so an index built earlier keeps the embedding model it was created with. Also, if you change the embedding model, rebuild or re-embed existing indexes so the vectors match.

`Settings` has other global options too, such as `chunk_size`, `chunk_overlap`, `context_window`, `num_output`, `transformations`, and `callback_manager`.

I'm not certain about the exact defaults or every parameter name in the latest release, since the API has changed across versions. Check the official LlamaIndex documentation for your installed version if something doesn't match.
